description: Detects systemd-udevd, running as root, spawning a shell, scripting interpreter, or file-permission utility - the root-code-execution step of the snap-confine LPE CVE-2026-8933.
references:
  - https://blog.qualys.com/vulnerabilities-threat-research/2026/07/21/cve-2026-8933-snap-confine-local-privilege-escalation
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/23
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1546
  - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: 'systemd-udevd'
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/python3'
      - '/perl'
      - '/nc'
      - '/ncat'
      - '/cp'
      - '/chmod'
      - '/chown'
  condition: selection
level: high
2657.spl: | tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="systemd-udevd" AND Processes.process_name IN ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","python3","perl","nc","ncat","cp","chmod","chown","id") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
2657.falcon:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/systemd-udevd/i
| ImageFileName=/\/(sh|bash|dash|zsh|python3|perl|nc|ncat|cp|chmod|chown|id)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

2661.def:

// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named

DeviceFileEvents

| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")

| tstats `summariesonly` count earliest(_time) AS firstTime latest(_time) AS lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process_name IN ("svcmgmt.exe"))

       Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_path

| tstats `summariesonly` count

       Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
]
